detail: T-CMD LIST (L, dev f2629613e, persvati cores 12-23, tmpfs, scale-1m, one client, a 2-group LIST): p50 1.15 s / 11.3 s / 29.0 s at 1k / 10k / 25k articles; owner CPU per LIST 58 / 820 / 3,086 ms. Mechanism A (wait): fn-lst was a def-cursor, so every host activation made ONE controller call (books/served-query-plan.lisp fn-qplan-rest-cursor-step-acc: 'exactly one accepted LIST controller call per activation'), and fn-lst-one probes one article number per call in phase :summary (books/group-summary-cursor.lisp fn-gsc-one); each empty activation yielded through fnn-mux-plan-yield with fn-splan-cursor-resume-ms = 1 ms, so the quantum count grew with the store (articles + phases + digits), not the reply. Mechanism B (CPU): the per-activation overhead (owner mutex, window activation, plan rebuild) dominates; the cursor itself carries its position (groups rest, gsc k) and is not re-walked. Fix: fn-lst-batch (def-cursor/batch) spends the visit grant per activation and fn-asto-resume-ms (ACL2) makes a LIST yield due on the next loop pass. Statements owed and discharged: fn-lst-batch-residual (what a batch emits followed by the residual of the cursor it returns is the residual it was given = the reference reply), fn-lst-batch-call-bound, fn-lst-batch-byte-bound, fn-asto-resume-ms-lst-is-immediate, fn-asto-resume-ms-over-waits. Measurement after the fix is owed on the same cell.
title: T-CMD LIST: a LIST costs one timer-paced owner activation per article probe (29 s p50 and 3.1 s owner CPU at 25k articles)
